blocks.content: Heat is a form of energy that flows from a body at higher temperature to a body at lower temperature. The study of heat and temperature is known as thermodynamics. Heat plays an important role in daily life, industrial processes and natural phenomena.
1. Meaning of Heat

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Heat is a form of energy transferred due to a temperature difference between two bodies.
Temperature measures the degree of hotness or coldness of a body and determines the direction of heat flow.
Conduction occurs mainly in solids without actual movement of particles, whereas convection occurs in fluids through direct particle movement.
Radiation does not require any material medium and transfers thermal energy at the speed of light via electromagnetic waves.
Water exhibits anomalous expansion between 0°C and 4°C, reaching its maximum density at 4°C.

blocks.content: • Heat is a form of energy that produces the sensation of warmth.
• It flows from a hotter object to a colder object.
• The SI unit of heat is Joule (J).
• Heat is a form of energy transfer.
2. Temperature
• Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
• It determines the direction of heat flow.
• Common temperature scales are Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin.
3. Temperature Scales
Heat is a form of energy that spontaneously flows from a body at a higher temperature to a body at a lower temperature.
4. Modes of Heat Transfer

cells: Transfer of heat through solids without movement of particles
Transfer of heat through liquids and gases by movement of particles
Transfer of heat through electromagnetic waves without medium

blocks.content: 5. Conduction
Conduction occurs mainly in solids where heat energy is transferred from one particle to another without the movement of the particles themselves.
6. Convection

rows: Vibration of adjacent particles without actual displacement
Actual bodily movement of heated fluid particles

blocks.content: Convection occurs in liquids and gases where heated particles move from one place to another carrying heat energy.
7. Radiation
Radiation is the transfer of heat in the form of electromagnetic waves. It does not require any material medium.
8. Effects of Heat
• Expansion of substances
• Change of state (solid, liquid, gas)
• Increase in temperature
9. Expansion due to Heat

items: Radiation is the only mode of heat transfer that can take place through a vacuum.
Water contracts when heated from 0°C to 4°C, resulting in maximum density at 4°C—a frequently asked concept in competitive exams.

blocks.content: When substances are heated, they expand. Expansion can occur in solids, liquids and gases.
Important Facts
• Heat flows from higher temperature to lower temperature.
• SI unit of heat is Joule.
• There are three modes of heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation.
• Radiation does not require a medium.
